body:
Filing gate: ③ task dispatched by the maintainer, quoted verbatim below; observation class (a), this session.
reach: `content/docs/getting-started/index.mdx` ("What is ObjectStack? — a 5-minute intro") is the docs landing for Getting Started; its nav (`meta.json`) lists, under "Start Here", `how-ai-development-works`, `build-with-claude-code`, `your-first-project`, `quick-start` (navTitle "Anatomy of an ObjectStack App"), `examples`. Each of the four pages opens with a callout pointing at one or two of the others.
Reader: `domain:devx` seat (`content/docs/getting-started/index.mdx`, the "How you'll build" section; optionally the four pages' opening callouts).
Dedup: `search_issues` "getting started pages overlap which page to start Build with Claude Code Your First Project Anatomy routing index" → 0 hits.
Filed on the maintainer's instruction in this session (category ③, quoted verbatim): 「Getting Started 四个入口页重叠。 How AI dev works / Build with Claude Code / Your First Project / Anatomy 相互引用,新人得自己选。建议 index 顶部一行分流:"想让 agent 写 → Build with Claude Code;想手写理解每个文件 → Your First Project"。」

## Today

Reading in nav order: *How AI development works* explains the loop and sends you to *Build with Claude Code*; *Build with Claude Code* says "want to understand the pieces first? read *Anatomy*"; *Your First Project* says "normally an agent authors the metadata — this page walks the same ground manually"; *Anatomy* says "want to build, not read? follow *Build with Claude Code*; new here? the *Examples*". All four are good pages; the problem is that the reader has to read the first paragraph of each to learn which one is theirs, and the index page's own "How you'll build" section offers two cards (Build with Claude Code, How AI development works) without saying when to pick the hand-written path.

## Asked for

One routing line (or a three-row table) at the top of the index, above the mermaid diagram, in the reader's own terms:

> **Start here:** want the agent to write the app → [Build with Claude Code]. Want to write it by hand and understand every file → [Your First Project]. Want to read what the agent wrote before you trust it → [Anatomy of an app]. Want the why first → [How AI development works].

And each of the four pages keeps exactly one cross-reference callout, pointing back at this line rather than at each other.
